studies.Study: Nomura AM et al. (2003) [PMID: 14501712] — estimate 1 · Male
studies.Reference: Serum vitamins and the subsequent risk of bladder cancer.
studies.Title: Serum vitamins and the subsequent risk of bladder cancer.
studies.Authors: Nomura AM, Lee J, Stemmermann GN, Franke AA
studies.Timing: Prospective, more than 20 years of surveillance

sample_size.excerpt: After a surveillance period of more than 20 years 111 tissue confirmed incident cases of bladder cancer were identified. Stored serum and that of 111 age matched controls were tested by high pressure liquid chromatography for certain micronutrients, including lutein, zeaxanthin, anhydrolutein, alpha-cryptoxanthin, beta-cryptoxanthin, lycopene, dihydrolycopene, alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, total carotenoids, retinol, alpha-tocopherol, beta-tocopherol, gamma-tocopherol, delta-tocopherol and total tocopherols.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 111 + 111 = 222

cases.excerpt: After a surveillance period of more than 20 years 111 tissue confirmed incident cases of bladder cancer were identified.

comparison.excerpt: Based on quartiles of serum micronutrient levels the ORs for bladder cancer were determined

design.excerpt: A cohort of 9,345 Japanese-American men was examined from 1971 to 1977

sample_size.excerpt: We performed a case-control study in 242 patients with bladder cancer and 204 healthy controls at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center from 1993 to 1997. Epidemiological data and blood specimens were collected on 84 cases and 173 controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 84 + 173 = 257

cases.excerpt: Epidemiological data and blood specimens were collected on 84 cases and 173 controls.

effect_size.excerpt: When using plasma levels of micronutrients as continuous variables, the adjusted OR was 0.22 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.92) for alpha-carotene, 0.42 (95% CI 0.18 to 1.00) for lutein, 0.16 (95% CI 0.02 to 1.06) for zeaxanthin, 0.94 (95% CI 0.89 to 0.99) for lycopene and 0.90 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.00) for beta-cryptoxanthin.

confidence_interval.excerpt: When using plasma levels of micronutrients as continuous variables, the adjusted OR was 0.22 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.92) for alpha-carotene, 0.42 (95% CI 0.18 to 1.00) for lutein, 0.16 (95% CI 0.02 to 1.06) for zeaxanthin, 0.94 (95% CI 0.89 to 0.99) for lycopene and 0.90 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.00) for beta-cryptoxanthin.

sample_size.excerpt: We investigated the association between plasma carotenoids and vitamin C and risk of urothelial cell carcinoma (UCC) in a case-control study nested within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition. A total of 856 patients with newly diagnosed UCC were matched with 856 cohort members by sex, age at baseline, study center, date and time of blood collection, and fasting status.
sample_size.location: Methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 856 + 856 = 1712
